title: The Case of the Bent Page
story: A book had a bent page. Mr. Ruiz looked in the bin. The book was at the bottom. Six big books sat on top of it. The page is bent, not torn. Ava read it on the rug. She did not bend it. A heavy stack can bend a page.
question: What bent the page?

suspects.why: six big books sat on it
she did not bend it
the page is bent, not torn

answer: The books on top bent the page.
proof: “Six big books sat on top of it.”
“A heavy stack can bend a page.”
clears: Ava: “She did not bend it.”
Cutting: “The page is bent, not torn.”
explain: The book was at the bottom of the bin. Because six big books sat on top, the heavy stack bent the page.

debate.story: A book had a bent page. The book was at the bottom of the bin. Six big books sat on top. A heavy stack can bend a page. Ava read it on the rug. She put it in her bag too. The bend has a sharp fold line.
debate.question: What bent the page? Point to the words.

suspects.why: six big books on top, and a stack can bend a page
read it on the rug and put it in her bag
a sharp fold line in the bend

evidence: “Six big books sat on top.”
“A heavy stack can bend a page.”
arguments.against: “She put it in her bag too.”

evidence: “Ava read it on the rug.”
“She put it in her bag too.”
“The bend has a sharp fold line.”
arguments.against: “A heavy stack can bend a page.”

debate.note: A stack makes a soft bend. A fold makes a sharp line. Let the children bend a page both ways on a scrap of paper and look at what they get.

title: The Case of the Smashed Sandwich
story: Leo opened his lunch box. His sandwich was flat. A big water bottle lay on top of it. The bottle is heavy and full. His mom packed it last. Nobody sat on the box. The bread is flat, not wet.
question: What smashed the sandwich?

suspects.why: it lay on top and is full
nobody sat on the box
the bread is flat, not wet

answer: The heavy bottle smashed the sandwich.
proof: “A big water bottle lay on top of it.”
clears: Sitting on it: “Nobody sat on the box.”
A leak: “The bread is flat, not wet.”
explain: The bread is flat, not wet. Because the heavy bottle lay on top of the sandwich, it pressed the bread flat.

debate.story: Leo opened his lunch box. His sandwich was flat. A big water bottle lay on top. The bottle is heavy and full. The box was under his backpack all morning. A wet ring sits under the bread.
debate.question: What flattened the sandwich? Show the words.

suspects.why: a heavy full bottle lying on top
the box under his backpack all morning
a wet ring under the bread

evidence: “A big water bottle lay on top.”
“The bottle is heavy and full.”
arguments.against: “The box was under his backpack all morning.”

evidence: “The box was under his backpack all morning.”
arguments.against: “A big water bottle lay on top.”

evidence: “A wet ring sits under the bread.”

debate.note: Two heavy things were on that sandwich and one of them was leaking. Ask which one was there longer, and whether a wet ring tells you about weight at all.

title: The Case of the Broken Tip
story: Ivy's pencil tip broke three times. She pressed very hard on the paper. The paper sat on a soft mat. A soft mat lets the tip sink. Her other pencils are fine. The lead is not cracked inside. She moved to a hard desk. The tip did not break.
question: Why did the tip keep breaking?

suspects.why: a soft mat lets the tip sink
the lead is not cracked inside
her other pencils are fine

answer: The soft mat let the tip sink and break.
proof: “The paper sat on a soft mat.”
“A soft mat lets the tip sink.”
clears: Cracked lead: “The lead is not cracked inside.”
Bad pencils: “Her other pencils are fine.”
explain: The tip did not break on a hard desk. Because the soft mat let the tip sink, the point broke when she pressed hard.

debate.story: Ivy's pencil tip broke three times. She pressed very hard on the paper. The paper sat on a soft mat. A soft mat lets the tip sink. Her pencil box fell down the stairs. Two new pencils broke the same way.
debate.question: Why does the tip keep breaking? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a soft mat that lets the tip sink
a pencil box that fell down the stairs
two new pencils that broke the same way

evidence: “The paper sat on a soft mat.”
“A soft mat lets the tip sink.”
arguments.against: “Her pencil box fell down the stairs.”

evidence: “Her pencil box fell down the stairs.”
arguments.against: “She pressed very hard on the paper.”

evidence: “Two new pencils broke the same way.”
arguments.against: “A soft mat lets the tip sink.”

debate.note: New pencils breaking the same way is the big clue. Ask whether that fits the mat, the fall, or both, and let somebody try a pencil on a hard desk.

title: The Case of the Brown Apple
story: Sam cut an apple at nine. By noon it was brown. He wrapped the other half up tight. That half is still white. Air turns a cut apple brown. Nobody touched the slices. The slices smell fine.
question: Why did the apple turn brown?

suspects.why: air turns a cut apple brown
nobody touched the slices
the slices smell fine

answer: Air turned the cut apple brown.
clears: Touching: “Nobody touched the slices.”
Going bad: “The slices smell fine.”
explain: The wrapped half is still white. Because air turns a cut apple brown, the half left open went brown by noon.

debate.story: Sam cut an apple at nine. By noon it was brown. He wrapped the other half up tight. That half is still white. Air turns a cut apple brown. The brown half sat on a warm sill. Three hands picked slices off it.
debate.question: Why did one half turn brown? Show the words.

suspects.why: air on the cut side, which turns an apple brown
three hands picking slices off it
sitting on a warm sill

evidence: “Air turns a cut apple brown.”
“He wrapped the other half up tight.”
arguments.against: “The brown half sat on a warm sill.”

evidence: “Three hands picked slices off it.”
“The brown half sat on a warm sill.”

debate.note: The wrapped half is the one to keep looking at. It had no air and no hands and no sun, and it is still white. Ask which of those three the wrapping kept away.

title: The Case of the Wobbly Seat
story: Dev's bike seat wobbled side to side. The bolt under the seat was loose. He did not crash. The frame is straight. A loose bolt lets a seat move. His dad turned the bolt tight. The seat stopped wobbling.
question: Why did the seat wobble?

suspects.why: the bolt under the seat was loose
he did not crash
the frame is straight

answer: A loose bolt let the seat wobble.
proof: “The bolt under the seat was loose.”
“A loose bolt lets a seat move.”
clears: A crash: “He did not crash.”
A bent frame: “The frame is straight.”
explain: The seat stopped wobbling after the bolt was tight. Because the bolt was loose, the seat could move side to side.

debate.story: Dev's bike seat wobbled side to side. The bolt under the seat was loose. A loose bolt lets a seat move. Dev dropped the bike on Friday. The seat post has a bend near the top. His dad turned the bolt tight.
debate.question: Why does the seat wobble? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a loose bolt under the seat
the bike dropped on Friday
a bend in the seat post near the top

evidence: “The bolt under the seat was loose.”
“A loose bolt lets a seat move.”
arguments.against: “The seat post has a bend near the top.”

evidence: “Dev dropped the bike on Friday.”
arguments.against: “A loose bolt lets a seat move.”

evidence: “The seat post has a bend near the top.”

debate.note: The story stops before telling us whether the wobble went away. Ask the class what they want to know next, and listen for the child who wants to ride it.

title: The Case of the Hiding Fish
story: The class fish hid behind a rock. It used to swim in front. A new big fish came on Monday. Big fish chase little fish. The water is clean. The food is the same. The little fish came out when the big one left.
question: Why did the little fish hide?

suspects.why: big fish chase little fish
the water is clean
the food is the same

answer: The new big fish made it hide.
proof: “A new big fish came on Monday.”
clears: Dirty water: “The water is clean.”
New food: “The food is the same.”
explain: The little fish came out when the big one left. Because big fish chase little fish, the new fish made it hide behind the rock.

debate.story: The class fish hid behind a rock. A new big fish came on Monday. Big fish chase little fish. The tank was moved to a bright shelf. A new bag of food was opened on Monday. The little fish came out at night.
debate.question: Why is the fish hiding? Show the words.

suspects.why: a big new fish, and big fish chase little ones
the tank moved to a bright shelf
a new bag of food opened on Monday

evidence: “A new big fish came on Monday.”
“Big fish chase little fish.”
arguments.against: “The tank was moved to a bright shelf.”

evidence: “The tank was moved to a bright shelf.”
arguments.against: “The little fish came out at night.”

evidence: “A new bag of food was opened on Monday.”

debate.note: Coming out at night is the clue. Ask what is different about the tank at night, and whether the big fish goes home when the lights go off.

title: The Case of the Tapping Window
story: A tap came from the window. It tapped only on windy days. A branch hangs near the glass. Wind pushes the branch. The branch hits the window. The tap came again at noon. No bird was there. The clock does not tap.
question: What tapped the window?

suspects.why: the branch hits the window
no bird was there
the clock does not tap

answer: A branch tapped the window in the wind.
clears: A bird: “No bird was there.”
The clock: “The clock does not tap.”
explain: It tapped only on windy days. Because wind pushes the branch, the branch hits the window.

debate.story: A tap came from the window. It tapped only on windy days. A branch hangs near the glass. Wind pushes the branch. A bird sits on that sill each day. The blind cord swings and knocks the glass.
debate.question: What is tapping? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a branch near the glass that the wind pushes
a bird on that sill each day
a blind cord that swings and knocks

evidence: “A branch hangs near the glass.”
“Wind pushes the branch.”
arguments.against: “A bird sits on that sill each day.”

evidence: “A bird sits on that sill each day.”
“The blind cord swings and knocks the glass.”

debate.note: Only on windy days is the sentence that sorts this out. A bird comes every day. Ask what makes a cord swing, and somebody will say the wind too.

title: The Case of the Leaf in the Hall
story: One red leaf sat in the hall. The door was open at recess. Wind blew in the open door. The leaf is from the big maple. The maple is by that door. No one carried it in. The leaf is not wet.
question: How did the leaf get inside?

suspects.why: the maple is by that door
no one carried it in
the leaf is not wet

answer: Wind blew the leaf in the open door.
clears: Carrying: “No one carried it in.”
Rain: “The leaf is not wet.”
explain: The leaf is from the big maple by that door. Because the door was open and wind blew in, the leaf came in on the wind.

debate.story: One red leaf sat in the hall. The door was open at recess. Wind blew in the open door. The maple is by that door. Kim came in with leaves on her coat. The leaf has a wet mark on it.
debate.question: How did the leaf get in? Show the words.

suspects.why: an open door with wind, and the maple beside it
leaves on Kim's coat when she came in
a wet mark on the leaf

evidence: “Wind blew in the open door.”
“The maple is by that door.”
arguments.against: “Kim came in with leaves on her coat.”

evidence: “Kim came in with leaves on her coat.”
“The leaf has a wet mark on it.”

debate.note: Both answers start at the same door, which is why this is hard and short. The wet mark is the odd one. Ask where a leaf gets wet, and whether the hall is wet anywhere.

title: The Case of the Pumpkin Seeds
story: Seeds were on the floor by the pumpkin. The pumpkin has a hole in the side. The hole has small tooth marks. A mouse was seen in the hall. No one cut the pumpkin. The class did not open it.
question: Who ate the pumpkin seeds?

suspects.why: the hole has small tooth marks
no one cut the pumpkin
the class did not open it

answer: A mouse chewed a hole and ate the seeds.
proof: “A mouse was seen in the hall.”
clears: Cutting: “No one cut the pumpkin.”
The class: “The class did not open it.”
explain: The hole has small tooth marks. Because a mouse was seen in the hall, a mouse chewed in and ate the seeds.

debate.story: Seeds were on the floor by the pumpkin. The pumpkin has a hole in the side. The hole has small tooth marks. A mouse was seen in the hall. The lid was lifted off on Friday. A knife sat beside the pumpkin all week.
debate.question: Who made the hole? Point to the words.

suspects.why: small tooth marks, and a mouse in the hall
a knife beside the pumpkin all week
the lid lifted off on Friday

evidence: “The hole has small tooth marks.”
“A mouse was seen in the hall.”
arguments.against: “A knife sat beside the pumpkin all week.”

evidence: “A knife sat beside the pumpkin all week.”
“The lid was lifted off on Friday.”
arguments.against: “The pumpkin has a hole in the side.”

debate.note: Teeth marks are teeth marks. A knife leaves a straight cut and lifting a lid leaves nothing at all in the side. Ask what each one would look like.

title: The Case of the Small Prints
story: Small muddy prints went to the door. They have four toes. A dog has four toes. The prints are too small for a shoe. The class cat stayed inside. A dog was in the yard. The prints go out the door.
question: Who left the muddy prints?

suspects.why: a dog has four toes
the class cat stayed inside
the prints are too small for a shoe

answer: A dog left the muddy prints.
clears: The cat: “The class cat stayed inside.”
A shoe: “The prints are too small for a shoe.”
explain: The prints have four toes and go out the door. Because a dog has four toes and a dog was in the yard, the dog left them.

debate.story: Small muddy prints went to the door. They have four toes. A dog has four toes. A cat has four toes too. The class cat was out of her box on Friday. The prints are as wide as two fingers.
debate.question: Who left the prints? Show the words.

suspects.why: four toes, and a dog has four
out of her box on Friday, and a cat has four too
prints as wide as two fingers

evidence: “A dog has four toes.”
“The class cat was out of her box on Friday.”
“A cat has four toes too.”
arguments.against: “Small muddy prints went to the door.”

evidence: “The prints are as wide as two fingers.”

debate.note: Four toes used to mean a dog and now it means a dog or a cat. That is the lesson. Hold up two fingers and ask whose foot is that size.

title: The Case of the Wrong Stop
story: Mia got off at the wrong stop. She was reading her book. She did not watch the street. The driver calls each stop. Mia did not hear him. Her stop is the next one. The bus was not late.
question: Why did Mia get off early?

suspects.why: she did not hear the driver
the bus was not late
the driver calls each stop

answer: Mia was reading and missed her stop.
clears: A late bus: “The bus was not late.”
No call: “The driver calls each stop.”
explain: Her stop is the next one. Because she was reading and did not hear the driver, she got off one stop early.

debate.story: Mia got off at the wrong stop. She was reading her book. She did not watch the street. The driver names every stop out loud. His voice was quiet that day. The bus ran ten minutes early that morning.
debate.question: Why did Mia get off early? Point to the words.

suspects.why: reading, and not watching the street
a bus that ran ten minutes early
a driver whose voice was quiet that day

evidence: “She was reading her book.”
“She did not watch the street.”
“The bus ran ten minutes early that morning.”
arguments.against: “The driver names every stop out loud.”

evidence: “His voice was quiet that day.”
arguments.against: “The driver names every stop out loud.”

debate.note: Three things went wrong at once and any one of them would have been fine on its own. Ask what Mia could do next time, and what the driver could do.

title: The Case of the Tipped Trophy
story: The class trophy fell on its side. The shelf is not level. It leans down to the left. The trophy fell to the left. No one bumped the shelf. The trophy is not broken. A level shelf holds a trophy up.
question: Why did the trophy tip over?

suspects.why: the trophy fell the way the shelf leans
no one bumped the shelf
the trophy is not broken

answer: The sloping shelf let the trophy tip over.
clears: Bumping: “No one bumped the shelf.”
Breaking: “The trophy is not broken.”
explain: The trophy fell the same way the shelf leans. Because the shelf is not level, the trophy tipped to the left.

debate.story: The class trophy fell on its side. The shelf is not level. It leans down to the left. The trophy fell to the left. The door bangs that wall each time. The trophy stands on a very small base.
debate.question: Why did the trophy fall? Show the words.

suspects.why: a shelf leaning left, and the trophy fell left
a door that bangs that wall each time
a very small base to stand on

evidence: “It leans down to the left.”
“The trophy fell to the left.”
arguments.against: “The door bangs that wall each time.”

evidence: “The door bangs that wall each time.”
“The trophy stands on a very small base.”

debate.note: It leans left and it fell left. Say both sentences one after the other and let the class hear them match. Then ask which way a bang would push it.

title: The Case of the Cold Plate
story: The food was hot in the pan. On the plate it went cold fast. The plates came from a cold shelf. A cold plate takes the heat. The pan was still hot. Nobody opened a window. The next plates were warmed first.
question: Why did the food go cold?

suspects.why: a cold plate takes the heat
the pan was still hot
nobody opened a window

answer: The cold plates took the heat from the food.
proof: “The plates came from a cold shelf.”
clears: The pan: “The pan was still hot.”
An open window: “Nobody opened a window.”
explain: The next plates were warmed first. Because the plates came from a cold shelf, they took the heat from the food.

debate.story: The food was hot in the pan. On the plate it went cold fast. The plates came from a cold shelf. A cold plate takes the heat. The pan sat off the heat for ten minutes. The door to the yard stood open.
debate.question: Why did the food go cold? Point to the words.

suspects.why: plates from a cold shelf, which take the heat
ten minutes off the heat
a door to the yard standing open

evidence: “The plates came from a cold shelf.”
“A cold plate takes the heat.”
arguments.against: “The pan sat off the heat for ten minutes.”

evidence: “The pan sat off the heat for ten minutes.”
arguments.against: “The food was hot in the pan.”

evidence: “The door to the yard stood open.”

debate.note: The food was hot in the pan, so whatever cooled it happened after the pan. Point at that sentence and ask the class what comes next in the story.

title: The Case of the Stuck Cupcakes
story: The cupcakes stuck to the pan. The class forgot the paper cups. Butter was not used either. Cake sticks to a bare pan. Each cup had the same batter. The next batch used paper cups. Those came out clean. The pan is not old.
question: Why did the cupcakes stick?

suspects.why: cake sticks to a bare pan
the pan is not old
each cup had the same batter

answer: The cupcakes stuck because the pan was bare.
clears: An old pan: “The pan is not old.”
Too much batter: “Each cup had the same batter.”
explain: The next batch used paper cups and came out clean. Because the class forgot the cups and used no butter, the cake stuck to the bare pan.

debate.story: The cupcakes stuck to the pan. The class forgot the paper cups. Butter was not used either. Cake sticks to a bare pan. The pan is black and scratched inside. Two cups were filled right to the top.
debate.question: Why did they stick? Show the words.

suspects.why: no paper cups and no butter, on a bare pan
a pan black and scratched inside
two cups filled right to the top

evidence: “The class forgot the paper cups.”
“Cake sticks to a bare pan.”
arguments.against: “The pan is black and scratched inside.”

evidence: “The pan is black and scratched inside.”
“Two cups were filled right to the top.”

debate.note: Two cups were overfilled and all of them stuck. Ask how many stuck and how many were too full. The numbers do not match, and a six-year-old can see that.

title: The Case of the Lost Mitten
story: Kim had two mittens at recess. She came in with one. The lost one has no clip. Her other mitten is clipped to her coat. A clip holds a mitten on. The lost one was in the snow. No one took it.
question: Why did one mitten get lost?

suspects.why: a clip holds a mitten on
no one took it
the lost one was in the snow

answer: The mitten with no clip fell off in the snow.
clears: Somebody taking it: “No one took it.”
The wash: “The lost one was in the snow.”
explain: Her other mitten is clipped to her coat and did not fall. Because the lost one had no clip, it came off in the snow.

debate.story: Kim had two mittens at recess. She came in with one. The lost one has no clip. A clip holds a mitten on. Two children have red mittens like hers. Her coat went in the wash last night.
debate.question: Where is the mitten? Point to the words.

suspects.why: no clip, and a clip holds a mitten on
two children with red mittens like hers
a coat that went in the wash last night

evidence: “The lost one has no clip.”
“A clip holds a mitten on.”
arguments.against: “Two children have red mittens like hers.”

evidence: “Two children have red mittens like hers.”
“Her coat went in the wash last night.”

debate.note: She had two at recess and one after, so it went missing outside. Say that slowly. It does not tell you where, and it does tell you when, which is already something.

title: The Case of the Soggy Roof
story: The gingerbread roof went soft. The house sat by the sink. Steam rises from the hot sink. Steam makes gingerbread soft. The walls are away from the sink. The walls are still hard. No one spilled water on it.
question: Why did the roof go soft?

suspects.why: steam makes gingerbread soft
no one spilled water on it
the walls are still hard

answer: Steam from the sink made the roof soft.
clears: A spill: “No one spilled water on it.”
The walls: “The walls are still hard.”
explain: The walls are away from the sink and are still hard. Because steam rises from the hot sink, the roof above it went soft.

debate.story: The gingerbread roof went soft. The house sat by the sink. Steam rises from the hot sink. Steam makes gingerbread soft. A cup was knocked over on that table. The roof piece was rolled thinner than the walls.
debate.question: Why did the roof go soft? Show the words.

suspects.why: steam from the hot sink, which softens gingerbread
a cup knocked over on that table
a roof rolled thinner than the walls

evidence: “Steam rises from the hot sink.”
“Steam makes gingerbread soft.”
arguments.against: “A cup was knocked over on that table.”

evidence: “A cup was knocked over on that table.”
“The roof piece was rolled thinner than the walls.”

debate.note: Steam goes up and water goes down, and the roof is the top of the house. Ask the class which one reaches a roof first.

title: The Case of the Dark String
story: A string of lights went dark. The plug was in the wall. The switch was turned off. A switch off means no power. Mr. Cole flipped the switch on. All the lights came on. No bulb was broken.
question: Why did the lights go dark?

suspects.why: a switch off means no power
the plug was in the wall
no bulb was broken

answer: The switch was turned off.
clears: The plug: “The plug was in the wall.”
A broken bulb: “No bulb was broken.”
explain: All the lights came on when the switch was flipped. Because the switch was off, the string had no power.

debate.story: A string of lights went dark. The switch was turned off. A switch off means no power. The plug hangs half out of the wall. One bulb near the plug looks black. Mr. Cole flipped the switch on.
debate.question: Why are the lights dark? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a switch turned off, which means no power
a plug hanging half out of the wall
one bulb near the plug looking black

evidence: “The switch was turned off.”
“A switch off means no power.”
arguments.against: “The plug hangs half out of the wall.”

evidence: “The plug hangs half out of the wall.”
“One bulb near the plug looks black.”

debate.note: Three things are wrong with one string of lights. The story stops before saying whether the lights came on. Ask the class what they would try first and why.

title: The Case of the Stopped Clock
story: The class clock stopped at ten. The hands do not move. Mr. Lee opened the back. The battery was green and old. An old battery stops a clock. Nothing holds the hands. The clock is not cracked. He put a new one in. The clock runs again.
question: Why did the clock stop?

suspects.why: an old battery stops a clock
nothing holds the hands
the clock is not cracked

answer: The old battery stopped the clock.
clears: Stuck hands: “Nothing holds the hands.”
A drop: “The clock is not cracked.”
explain: The clock runs again with a new battery. Because the old battery was green and dead, the clock stopped.

debate.story: The class clock stopped at ten. The hands do not move. The battery was green and old. An old battery stops a clock. The clock fell off the wall last week. A bent hand catches on the glass.
debate.question: Why did the clock stop? Show the words.

suspects.why: a green old battery, which stops a clock
a bent hand that catches on the glass
the clock falling off the wall last week

evidence: “The battery was green and old.”
“An old battery stops a clock.”
arguments.against: “The clock fell off the wall last week.”

evidence: “A bent hand catches on the glass.”
“The clock fell off the wall last week.”

debate.note: A fall could bend a hand, so two of these answers may be one answer. Ask whether the fall and the bent hand are the same story told twice.

title: The Case of the Small Snowball
story: Max made a big snowball. He left it on the step. By lunch it was small. The step is in the sun. Sun melts snow fast. No one kicked it. A wet ring sits around it.
question: Why did the snowball get small?

suspects.why: sun melts snow fast
no one kicked it
a wet ring sits around it

answer: The sun melted the snowball.
clears: Kicking: “No one kicked it.”
A dog: “A wet ring sits around it.”
explain: A wet ring sits around it. Because the step is in the sun, the sun melted the snowball into water.

debate.story: Max made a big snowball. He left it on the step. By lunch it was small. The step is in the sun. Sun melts snow fast. A ring of wet stone sits around it. Boot marks cross the step. A dog ran past at ten.
debate.question: Why did the snowball get small? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a sunny step, and sun melts snow fast
boot marks crossing the step
a dog that ran past at ten

evidence: “The step is in the sun.”
“A ring of wet stone sits around it.”
“Boot marks cross the step.”
“A dog ran past at ten.”
arguments.against: “A ring of wet stone sits around it.”

debate.note: A wet ring is melted snow and it is still there. Ask where the snow went in each story. If a boot or a dog took it, where is it now?

title: The Case of the Spilled Seed
story: Seed lay under the bird feeder. The feeder has a big crack. Seed falls out of the crack. The lid was still shut tight. No squirrel was seen. Birds do not crack plastic. Mr. Lee taped the crack. The seed stopped falling.
question: Why was seed on the ground?

suspects.why: seed falls out of the crack
no squirrel was seen
birds do not crack plastic

answer: Seed fell out of the crack.
clears: A squirrel: “No squirrel was seen.”
The birds: “Birds do not crack plastic.”
explain: The seed stopped falling after the tape went on. Because the feeder has a big crack, the seed fell out of it.

debate.story: Seed lay under the bird feeder. The feeder has a big crack. Seed falls out of the crack. The lid was found open on Tuesday. Claw marks run down the pole. Birds push seed out while they eat.
debate.question: Why is seed on the ground? Show the words.

suspects.why: a big crack that seed falls out of
claw marks down the pole, and a lid found open
birds pushing seed out while they eat

evidence: “The feeder has a big crack.”
“Seed falls out of the crack.”
“Claw marks run down the pole.”
“The lid was found open on Tuesday.”
“Birds push seed out while they eat.”
arguments.against: “The lid was found open on Tuesday.”

debate.note: A crack spills seed in one spot. A squirrel spills it everywhere. Ask the class to look at where the seed is, not just that it is there.

title: The Case of the Spotted Cocoa
story: White spots floated on the cocoa. The milk came from a new jug. The jug sat out all night. Warm milk goes bad and makes spots. The cocoa mix was fresh. The cup was clean. The spots smell sour.
question: Why were there spots in the cocoa?

suspects.why: warm milk goes bad and makes spots
the cocoa mix was fresh
the cup was clean

answer: The milk went bad sitting out.
proof: “Warm milk goes bad and makes spots.”
clears: The mix: “The cocoa mix was fresh.”
A dirty cup: “The cup was clean.”
explain: The spots smell sour. Because the jug sat out all night, the warm milk went bad and made spots.

debate.story: White spots floated on the cocoa. The milk came from a new jug. The jug sat out all night. Warm milk goes bad and makes spots. The spots smell sour. The mix came from the bottom of the tin. The cup had been used for paint water.
debate.question: What made the spots? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a jug left out all night, and warm milk makes spots
mix from the bottom of the tin
a cup that had held paint water

evidence: “The jug sat out all night.”
“The spots smell sour.”
arguments.against: “The mix came from the bottom of the tin.”

evidence: “The mix came from the bottom of the tin.”
arguments.against: “Warm milk goes bad and makes spots.”

evidence: “The cup had been used for paint water.”

debate.note: Sour is a smell and it belongs to milk. Let the children say what sour means. Lumps from the bottom of a tin do not smell of anything.

title: The Case of the Blank Valentine
story: Ana got a valentine with no name. The card has a heart sticker. Only Jon has heart stickers. Jon sits next to Ana. Mia uses star stickers. Sam was home sick. Ana said thank you to Jon.
question: Who gave Ana the valentine?

suspects.why: only Jon has heart stickers
Mia uses star stickers
Sam was home sick

answer: Jon gave Ana the valentine.
clears: Mia: “Mia uses star stickers.”
Sam: “Sam was home sick.”
explain: Only Jon has heart stickers. Because the card has a heart sticker, Jon is the one who gave it.

debate.story: Ana got a valentine with no name. The card has a heart sticker. Only Jon has heart stickers. Jon sits next to Ana. Mia borrowed Jon's stickers on Friday. Sam sent his cards from home this year.
debate.question: Who sent the card? Show the words.

suspects.why: the only one with heart stickers, sitting next to Ana
borrowed Jon's stickers on Friday
sent his cards from home this year

evidence: “Only Jon has heart stickers.”
“Jon sits next to Ana.”
“Mia borrowed Jon's stickers on Friday.”
“Sam sent his cards from home this year.”

debate.note: Only Jon has heart stickers was the whole answer, and borrowing breaks it. Ask the class what only means once somebody has borrowed them.

title: The Case of the Flat Volcano
story: Rosa's volcano made no foam. She used baking powder by mistake. The jar says baking powder. Baking soda makes the foam. Her vinegar was new. The cup had no cracks. She tried it again. The right jar worked.
question: Why did the volcano make no foam?

suspects.why: baking soda makes the foam
her vinegar was new
the cup had no cracks

answer: She used baking powder, not baking soda.
clears: Old vinegar: “Her vinegar was new.”
A cracked cup: “The cup had no cracks.”
explain: The right jar worked when she tried again. Because she used baking powder and not baking soda, the volcano made no foam.

debate.story: Rosa's volcano made no foam. She used baking powder by mistake. Baking soda makes the foam. Her vinegar bottle had no lid for a week. She poured in one small spoon of vinegar. The cup is wide and low.
debate.question: Why was there no foam? Point to the words.

suspects.why: baking powder instead of soda, and soda makes the foam
one small spoon of vinegar
a cup that is wide and low

evidence: “She used baking powder by mistake.”
“Baking soda makes the foam.”
arguments.against: “She poured in one small spoon of vinegar.”

evidence: “She poured in one small spoon of vinegar.”
“The cup is wide and low.”

debate.note: No foam at all is the thing to hold on to. A small spoon makes a little foam. A wide cup makes low foam. Only the wrong powder makes none.

title: The Case of the Torn Crown
story: The paper crown has a long rip. It hung on a hook all night. The hook has a sharp end. Paper rips on a sharp end. No one wore it last night. The rip is at the hook spot. It is not cut straight.
question: What ripped the crown?

suspects.why: the rip is at the hook spot
no one wore it last night
it is not cut straight

answer: The sharp hook ripped the crown.
proof: “The rip is at the hook spot.”
clears: Wearing it: “No one wore it last night.”
Scissors: “It is not cut straight.”
explain: The rip is at the hook spot. Because the hook has a sharp end, the paper ripped on it.

debate.story: The paper crown has a long rip. It hung on a hook all night. The hook has a sharp end. Paper rips on a sharp end. The rip is at the hook spot. Two children tried it on at home time. The crown is made of thin paper.
debate.question: What tore the crown? Show the words.

suspects.why: a sharp hook, and the rip is at the hook spot

suspects.who: 🙋 The two who tried it on
suspects.why: two children who tried it on at home time
a crown made of thin paper

evidence: “The hook has a sharp end.”
“The rip is at the hook spot.”
arguments.against: “Two children tried it on at home time.”

evidence: “Two children tried it on at home time.”
arguments.against: “The rip is at the hook spot.”

evidence: “The crown is made of thin paper.”

debate.note: The rip is at the hook spot is the sentence that does the work. Ask where a rip would be if somebody pulled it on, and have a child show you on their own head.

title: The Case of the Stuck Key
story: One piano key will not go down. Mr. Lee looked inside. A coin sits under that key. A coin blocks a key. The other keys work fine. No one spilled water. He took the coin out. The key works now.
question: Why would one key not go down?

suspects.why: a coin blocks a key
no one spilled water
the other keys work fine

answer: A coin was stuck under the key.
clears: Water: “No one spilled water.”
A broken piano: “The other keys work fine.”
explain: The key works now that the coin is out. Because a coin sat under it, the key could not go down.

debate.story: One piano key will not go down. Mr. Lee looked inside. A coin sits under that key. A coin blocks a key. The key beside it is slow too. Something sticky was spilled on that end last week.
debate.question: Why will the key not go down? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a coin sitting under that key
something sticky spilled on that end last week
the key beside it is slow too

evidence: “A coin sits under that key.”
“A coin blocks a key.”
arguments.against: “The key beside it is slow too.”

evidence: “Something sticky was spilled on that end last week.”
“The key beside it is slow too.”

debate.note: One coin cannot sit under two keys. The key beside it is the clue that opens the case up. Ask how many keys are wrong and how many coins there are.

title: The Case of the Grounded Kite
story: Sam's kite would not fly. There was no wind today. A kite needs wind to fly. His string is not tangled. The kite has no rips. Lin's kite did not fly either. The flags hang straight down.
question: Why would the kite not fly?

suspects.why: the flags hang straight down
his string is not tangled
the kite has no rips

answer: There was no wind to lift the kite.
clears: A tangled string: “His string is not tangled.”
A rip: “The kite has no rips.”
explain: Lin's kite did not fly either. Because there was no wind, no kite could go up.

debate.story: Sam's kite would not fly. The flags hang straight down. A kite needs wind to fly. Lin's kite did not fly either. Sam's string is wound round the stick. The kite is bigger than last year's.
debate.question: Why would the kite not fly? Show the words.

suspects.why: flags hanging straight down, and a kite needs wind
string still wound round the stick
a kite bigger than last year's

evidence: “The flags hang straight down.”
“Lin's kite did not fly either.”
arguments.against: “Sam's string is wound round the stick.”

evidence: “Sam's string is wound round the stick.”
“The kite is bigger than last year's.”

debate.note: Lin's kite did not fly either, and Lin's string is not Sam's string. Two kites failing at once points at the sky rather than at either kite.

title: The Case of the Dry Shamrock
story: The shamrock leaves went limp. The pot soil is very dry. Plants need water to stand up. The class was away all week. No one watered it. The leaves are green, not brown. Water made it stand up again.
question: Why did the leaves go limp?

suspects.why: the pot soil is very dry
the leaves are green, not brown
water made it stand up again

answer: The plant had no water for a week.
clears: Bugs: “The leaves are green, not brown.”
Bad soil: “Water made it stand up again.”
explain: Water made it stand up again. Because the class was away all week, no one watered it and the soil went dry.

debate.story: The shamrock leaves went limp. The pot soil is very dry. Plants need water to stand up. The class was away all week. The pot sits right on the hot pipe. The leaves are pale at the edges.
debate.question: Why did the leaves go limp? Point to the words.

suspects.why: very dry soil, and plants need water to stand up
a pot sitting right on the hot pipe
leaves that are pale at the edges

evidence: “The pot soil is very dry.”
“The class was away all week.”
arguments.against: “The pot sits right on the hot pipe.”

evidence: “The pot sits right on the hot pipe.”
“The leaves are pale at the edges.”

debate.note: Dry soil and a hot pipe are close friends, and the class may well say so. Ask what dried the soil out, and the two answers join into one.

title: The Case of the Wet Boot
story: Theo's left boot is wet inside. His right boot is dry. He stepped in a deep puddle. The left boot has a hole. Water gets in through a hole. He did not spill his drink. The sock on that foot is wet.
question: Why is one boot wet inside?

suspects.why: water gets in through a hole
he did not spill his drink
his right boot is dry

answer: Water came in through the hole.
clears: A spilled drink: “He did not spill his drink.”
Rain: “His right boot is dry.”
explain: The sock on that foot is wet. Because the left boot has a hole, water got in when he stepped in the puddle.

debate.story: Theo's left boot is wet inside. The right boot is dry inside. He stepped in a deep puddle. The left boot has a hole. Water gets in through a hole. His left sock was wet when he put it on. The left boot was by the open window all night.
debate.question: Why is one boot wet inside? Show the words.

suspects.why: a hole in that boot, and water gets in through a hole
a left sock that was wet when he put it on
the left boot by the open window all night

evidence: “The left boot has a hole.”
“He stepped in a deep puddle.”
arguments.against: “His left sock was wet when he put it on.”

evidence: “His left sock was wet when he put it on.”
“The left boot was by the open window all night.”

debate.note: Everything in this story happened to the left foot. Say that out loud and count them on fingers. Three reasons and one wet boot.

title: The Case of the Missing Carrot Tops
story: The carrot tops are gone. The carrots are still in the dirt. Small tracks go to the fence. A rabbit hole is by the fence. Rabbits eat green tops. No one picked the carrots. The tracks are not shoe prints.
question: What ate the carrot tops?

suspects.why: rabbits eat green tops
no one picked the carrots
the tracks are not shoe prints

answer: A rabbit ate the carrot tops.
proof: “A rabbit hole is by the fence.”
clears: Picking: “No one picked the carrots.”
A person: “The tracks are not shoe prints.”
explain: The carrots are still in the dirt. Because a rabbit hole is by the fence and rabbits eat green tops, a rabbit ate them.

debate.story: The carrot tops are gone. The carrots are still in the dirt. Small tracks go to the fence. A rabbit hole is by the fence. Rabbits eat green tops. The class picked tops for the art table on Friday. A bird was seen pulling at the leaves.
debate.question: Where did the tops go? Point to the words.

suspects.why: small tracks to a rabbit hole, and rabbits eat tops
tops picked for the art table on Friday
a bird seen pulling at the leaves

evidence: “Small tracks go to the fence.”
“A rabbit hole is by the fence.”
arguments.against: “The class picked tops for the art table on Friday.”

evidence: “The class picked tops for the art table on Friday.”
“A bird was seen pulling at the leaves.”

debate.note: The carrots are still in the dirt, so whatever took the tops left the roots. Ask which of the three would do that, and whether anybody checked the art table.

title: The Case of the Broken Shell
story: A shell lay under the nest. The shell is in two neat halves. A chick pushes out in halves. A smashed egg is in bits. A new bird sits in the nest. No cat came near. The nest is not torn.
question: What happened to the egg?

suspects.why: a chick pushes out in halves
no cat came near
the nest is not torn

answer: A chick hatched out of the egg.
proof: “The shell is in two neat halves.”
clears: A cat: “No cat came near.”
Falling: “The nest is not torn.”
explain: A new bird sits in the nest. Because the shell is in two neat halves, a chick pushed its way out.

debate.story: A shell lay under the nest. The shell is in two neat halves. A chick pushes out in halves. A smashed egg is in bits. A new bird sits in the nest. A cat was under the tree on Monday. The nest leans to one side now.
debate.question: What happened to the egg? Show the words.

suspects.why: two neat halves, and a chick pushes out in halves
a cat under the tree on Monday
a nest that leans to one side now

evidence: “The shell is in two neat halves.”
“A new bird sits in the nest.”
arguments.against: “A cat was under the tree on Monday.”

evidence: “A cat was under the tree on Monday.”
“The nest leans to one side now.”

debate.note: Two neat halves and a new bird in the nest is a story that tells itself. Ask what the shell would look like if the cat had got it, and the word bits is already on the page.

title: The Case of the Full Bin
story: The paper bin fills up fast. The class cuts paper every day. Scraps go in the paper bin. The trash bin is almost empty. No one moved the bins. The scraps are all paper. Mrs. Diaz got a bigger bin.
question: Why does the paper bin fill up fast?

suspects.why: scraps go in the paper bin
no one moved the bins
the scraps are all paper

answer: Paper scraps from cutting fill the bin.
clears: The wrong bin: “No one moved the bins.”
Food scraps: “The scraps are all paper.”
explain: The trash bin is almost empty. Because the class cuts paper every day, the scraps fill the paper bin fast.

debate.story: The paper bin fills up fast. The class cuts paper every day. Scraps go in the paper bin. The trash bin is almost empty. The paper bin is the smaller of the two. Nobody empties it until Friday.
debate.question: Why does the paper bin fill up? Point to the words.

suspects.why: cutting paper every day, with scraps going in
the smaller of the two bins
nobody emptying it until Friday

evidence: “The class cuts paper every day.”
“Scraps go in the paper bin.”
arguments.against: “The paper bin is the smaller of the two.”

evidence: “The paper bin is the smaller of the two.”
“Nobody empties it until Friday.”

debate.note: One bin is full and one is empty, and they are different sizes and emptied at different times. Ask the class for the easiest thing to change, and let them argue about it.

title: The Case of the Half Photo
story: Half of the class photo is dark. A finger shape sits in the corner. Ben held the camera. His finger was over the lens. A finger blocks the light. The lens is clean. The battery was full.
question: Why is half the photo dark?

suspects.why: a finger blocks the light
the lens is clean
the battery was full

answer: Ben's finger covered part of the lens.
clears: A dirty lens: “The lens is clean.”
The battery: “The battery was full.”
explain: A finger shape sits in the corner. Because Ben's finger was over the lens, it blocked the light on that side.

debate.story: Half of the class photo is dark. A finger shape sits in the corner. Ben held the camera. A finger blocks the light. The room light was off on that side. Ben's thumb has a plaster on it today.
debate.question: Why is half the photo dark? Show the words.

suspects.why: a finger shape in the corner, and a finger blocks light
the room light off on that side
a plaster on Ben's thumb today

evidence: “A finger shape sits in the corner.”
“A finger blocks the light.”
arguments.against: “The room light was off on that side.”

evidence: “The room light was off on that side.”
arguments.against: “A finger shape sits in the corner.”

evidence: “Ben's thumb has a plaster on it today.”

debate.note: A finger shape is a shape, and shapes are the best evidence a six-year-old can use. Ask what a dark room looks like in a photo, and whether it has edges.

title: The Case of the Tall Bean
story: Two beans grew in one pot. One bean is tall and thin. It grew behind a big book. A plant stretches to find light. The short bean sits in the light. Both got the same water. Both have the same soil.
question: Why is one bean tall and thin?

suspects.why: a plant stretches to find light
both got the same water
both have the same soil

answer: The book blocked the light, so the bean stretched.
clears: Water: “Both got the same water.”
Soil: “Both have the same soil.”
explain: The short bean sits in the light. Because the tall bean grew behind a big book, it stretched up to find light.

debate.story: Two beans grew in one pot. One bean is tall and thin. It grew behind a big book. A plant stretches to find light. The short bean sits in the light. The tall one is closest to the warm wall. The tall seed went in three days first.
debate.question: Why is one bean tall and thin? Point to the words.

suspects.why: grown behind a big book, where a plant stretches for light
closest to the warm wall
a seed that went in three days first

evidence: “It grew behind a big book.”
“A plant stretches to find light.”
arguments.against: “The tall one is closest to the warm wall.”

evidence: “The tall one is closest to the warm wall.”
arguments.against: “The short bean sits in the light.”

evidence: “The tall seed went in three days first.”

debate.note: Tall and thin is two words and they do different jobs. A head start makes a plant taller. Only stretching for light makes it thin as well.

title: The Case of the Drippy Cone
story: Nia's cone dripped all over her hand. Jo's cone did not drip. Nia sat in the sun. Jo sat under the tree. Sun melts ice cream fast. Both cones were the same size. Both came from one tub.
question: Why did one cone drip?

suspects.why: sun melts ice cream fast
both cones were the same size
both came from one tub

answer: The sun melted Nia's ice cream.
clears: A bigger cone: “Both cones were the same size.”
Bad ice cream: “Both came from one tub.”
explain: Jo sat under the tree and her cone did not drip. Because Nia sat in the sun, her ice cream melted fast.

debate.story: Nia's cone dripped all over her hand. Jo's cone did not drip. Nia sat in the sun. Jo sat under the tree. Sun melts ice cream fast. Nia held hers for ten minutes before eating. Jo's cone came out of the tub last.
debate.question: Why did one cone drip? Show the words.

suspects.why: sitting in the sun, which melts ice cream fast
held for ten minutes before eating
a cone scooped out of the tub last

evidence: “Nia sat in the sun.”
“Jo sat under the tree.”
arguments.against: “Nia held hers for ten minutes before eating.”

evidence: “Nia held hers for ten minutes before eating.”
“Jo's cone came out of the tub last.”

debate.note: Nia was in the sun and she also waited. Ask what would have happened if Jo had waited ten minutes under the tree. That is the test, and the class can picture it.

title: The Case of the Short Ribbon
story: Kim's field day ribbon is short. The end is cut straight across. Scissors make a straight cut. The art box was open. A ribbon piece sits in the box. No one pulled on it. A rip is never straight.
question: Why is the ribbon short?

suspects.why: scissors make a straight cut
no one pulled on it
a rip is never straight

answer: Somebody cut the ribbon with scissors.
clears: Pulling: “No one pulled on it.”
A rip: “A rip is never straight.”
explain: A ribbon piece sits in the art box. Because the end is cut straight across, scissors made the cut.

debate.story: Kim's field day ribbon is short. The end is cut straight across. Scissors make a straight cut. A ribbon piece sits in the art box. Kim's ribbon was caught in the door at lunch. The ribbons came in two lengths this year.
debate.question: Why is the ribbon short? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a straight cut end, and scissors cut straight
caught in the door at lunch
ribbons that came in two lengths this year

evidence: “The end is cut straight across.”
“A ribbon piece sits in the art box.”
arguments.against: “Kim's ribbon was caught in the door at lunch.”

evidence: “Kim's ribbon was caught in the door at lunch.”
“The ribbons came in two lengths this year.”

debate.note: If the ribbons came in two lengths, maybe nothing happened at all. That is a good answer and children rarely reach it. The straight end is the thing that argues back.

title: The Case of the Loud Pop
story: A balloon popped by the window. The window sill is hot. Hot air makes a balloon grow. A grown balloon pops. The balloons in the shade are fine. No pin was in the room. No one touched them.
question: Why did the balloon pop?

suspects.why: hot air makes a balloon grow
no pin was in the room
no one touched them

answer: Heat made the balloon grow and pop.
clears: A pin: “No pin was in the room.”
Somebody popping it: “No one touched them.”
explain: The balloons in the shade are fine. Because the window sill is hot, the air inside grew and the balloon popped.

debate.story: A balloon popped by the window. The window sill is hot. Hot air makes a balloon grow. A grown balloon pops. The balloons in the shade are fine. The window balloons were blown up the biggest. A staple holds the string to the sill.
debate.question: Why did the balloon pop? Show the words.

suspects.why: a hot sill, and hot air makes a balloon grow
the window balloons blown up the biggest
a staple holding the string to the sill

evidence: “The window sill is hot.”
“The balloons in the shade are fine.”
arguments.against: “The window balloons were blown up the biggest.”

evidence: “The window balloons were blown up the biggest.”
arguments.against: “The balloons in the shade are fine.”

evidence: “A staple holds the string to the sill.”

debate.note: The shade balloons are fine, and that one sentence is worth more than the rest. They are in the same room with the same staples. Ask what is different about them.
